title: Terraform security overlays for private VPC: SGs, NACLs, private DNS, and egress controls
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description:
Summary: Create a reusable Terraform module (redwood_vpc_security_overlay) to centralize security controls for Private/VPC deployments. The module will manage security groups (least-privilege defaults + role-based templates), stateless and stateful NACL overlays, private Route53 hosted zones + resolver rules, controlled egress via NAT/egress proxies and allowlists, and recommended VPC endpoints (S3, STS). It must be idempotent, audit-friendly, and support rolling upgrades with a migration path for existing customers.

Goals:
- Provide an opinionated, secure default surface that can be overridden via inputs.
- Support cross-account/private control-plane scenarios (Route53 resolver inbound endpoints).
- Expose structured outputs so higher-level stacks can consume SG IDs, NACL IDs, and resolver rule IDs.
- Built-in health checks and drift detection hooks to surface misconfigurations to Console.
- Upgrade plan that avoids connection loss: blue/green application for SG/NACL changes where possible, staged resolver updates.

Acceptance criteria:
- Module published to internal Terraform registry with versioned releases and changelog.
- Integration tests run in ephemeral CI env: validate provisioning, policy enforcement, DNS resolution from private subnets, egress path control, and NACL rule ordering behavior.
- Canary rollout documented and runbook created for migrations.
- Security review completed and audit logs emitted to central logging.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Security groups are preferred for fine-grained instance-level control; NACLs used for perimeter-level stateless protections and to economically mitigate noisy attack patterns. Module will create SG templates for "control-plane", "worker", and "egress-proxy" with default deny ingress and minimal required egress.
- NACLs implemented as overlay resources using an explicit ordering scheme: module manages a high-priority set that applies protective rules before existing NACLs to avoid surprise broad allow rules. This avoids destructive reordering of customer managed rules.
- Private DNS: use Route53 private hosted zones when customers opt-in; otherwise, create resolver rules pointing to internal resolver endpoints. Resolver inbound/outbound endpoints are optional and gated behind an input allowing cross-account forwarding.
- Egress control: support three modes via input: "open" (default for P0 internal deployments), "proxy" (route egress through an autoscaled HTTP/HTTPS proxy EC2/ALB or managed egress appliance), and "allowlist" (explicit managed allowlist of CIDR or FQDNs implemented via proxy + egress security groups). For managed allowlist we provide integration hooks to the console's allowlist API.
- Compatibility: Keep interfaces simple (primitive types and maps). Avoid embedding provider-specific lifecycle hacks; use stable Terraform features to maintain cross-version compatibility.

Upgrade & migration plan:
- Provide a migration script (terraform plan + validation runner) that runs against customer's state: it will detect whether NACL ordering changes, SG replacement, or resolver updates are required and classify operations as "safe" or "disruptive".
- For disruptive changes (e.g., SG replacement that would drop active connections), default to creating new resources and attaching them to instances in a staged manner, followed by detaching old ones after health checks pass.
- Document rollback steps and include automated snapshots of original resource IDs for quick rollback.

Health checks and observability:
- Module injects optional CloudWatch/Prometheus metrics via a small Lambda that performs synthetic checks: DNS resolution for private hosted zones, egress request success rate through proxy, and security group rule drift checks.
- Expose an outputs map that includes a health_check_endpoint, resolver_rule_id, list_of_created_resources, and a module_version tag on resources for tracking.
- Emit structured Terraform outputs compatible with Console's resource inventory ingestion.

Testing plan:
- Unit: terratest/Go and kitchen-terraform scenarios for primary permutations (proxy/on/off, private-dns on/off, cross-account resolver).
- CI: ephemeral AWS account in CircleCI with post-provision connectivity tests, DNS queries, and egress verification.
- Pre-release: run against one Dedicated customer staging VPC as a canary.

Docs & runbook:
- Confluence PRD + module README with example usage patterns and migration checklist.
- Runbook pages: manual rollback, emergency open-egress switch, and diagnostics (how to validate DNS resolver endpoints and NACL order).
